'''Richard L. Doty''' is a professor of [[psychology]] and [[otorhinolaryngology]] at the [[University of Pennsylvania]]. He has also been the director of the University of Pennsylvania's Smell and Taste Center since 1980.

Doty is considered a world-renowned researcher in the field of [[olfaction|olfactory]] functioning and dysfunction ([[anosmia]]). He is a pioneer in the development and validation of practical quantitative tests of olfaction, including the [[University of Pennsylvania Smell Identification Test]] (UPSIT).<ref name="penn-bio">{{Cite web |title=Richard L. Doty - Faculty Biosketch |url=https://www.med.upenn.edu/apps/faculty/index.php/g329/p9720 |access-date=2024-11-30 |website=University of Pennsylvania}}</ref>{{Primary source inline|date=November 2024}}

== Career ==

Doty received his Bachelor of Science degree from [[Colorado State University]] in 1966. He was awarded a Master of Arts in experimental psychology with an emphasis in [[psychophysics]] from [[California State University San Jose]] in conjunction with [[NASA]]’s [[Ames Research Center]] in 1968. Doty earned his Ph.D. in Comparative Psychology and Zoology from [[Michigan State University]] in 1971.<ref name = penn-bio/>{{Primary source inline|date=November 2024}}

He was a [[postdoctoral]] research fellow at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] from 1971 to 1973 in the field of behavioral [[endocrinology]] and was advised by [[Frank A. Beach|Dr. Frank Beach]]. At the [[Monell Chemical Senses Center]] in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, he was a Postdoctoral Fellow from 1973-1974 and then Director of the Human Olfaction Section from 1974-1978.<ref name = penn-bio/>{{Primary source inline|date=November 2024}}

Doty created the [[University of Pennsylvania Smell Identification Test]] (UPSIT).<ref name = ajol1>{{cite journal |last1=Doty |first1=Richard |last2=Mackay-Sim |first2=A |title=University of Pennsylvania smell identification test |date=October 2001 |journal=Australian Journal of Oto-Laryngology |access-date=March 8, 2010 |via=[[FindArticles]] |url=http://www.findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_qa3868/is_200110/ai_n8959365 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050320150424/http://www.findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_qa3868/is_200110/ai_n8959365 |archive-date=March 20, 2005 |url-status=usurped}}</ref>

Doty has published over 400 papers in peer-reviewed journals related to olfactory and gustatory function,{{citation needed|date=December 2020}} and is the editor or author of nine books, including ''Handbook of Olfaction and Gustation'',<ref name=":0" /> ''Neurology of Olfaction'' with Christopher Hawkes<!-- Not [[Christopher Hawkes]]. -->,<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Jellinger |first=K. A. |date=July 2009 |title=The Neurology of Olfaction |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1468-1331.2009.02683.x |journal=European Journal of Neurology |language=en |volume=16 |issue=7 |pages=e141 |doi=10.1111/j.1468-1331.2009.02683.x|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and ''[[The Great Pheromone Myth]],<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last=Baker |first=Ann Eileen Miller |date=September 2011 |title=The Great Pheromone Myth . By Richard L. Doty. Baltimore (Maryland): Johns Hopkins University Press. $65.00. xiii + 278 p.; ill.; name and subject indexes. {{text|ISBN}}: 978-0-8018-9347-6. 2010. |url=https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/10.1086/661121 |journal=The Quarterly Review of Biology |language=en |volume=86 |issue=3 |pages=231 |doi=10.1086/661121 |issn=0033-5770|url-access=subscription }}</ref>'' among others.

== Awards ==
{{BLP unreferenced section|date=November 2024}}
Doty has received multiple awards. In 1996, he received a [[James A. Shannon]] Award from the [[National Institutes of Health]]. Doty received the Olfactory Research Fund's Scientific Sense of Smell Award in 2000. In 2003 he received the [[William Osler]] Patient-Oriented Research Award from the University of Pennsylvania. 2004 saw Doty receive the [[Society of Cosmetic Chemists|Society of Cosmetic Chemists’]] Service Award. A year later in 2005 he was recognized by the [[Association for Chemoreception Sciences]] with the Max Mozell Award for Outstanding Achievement in the Chemical Senses.
